gaps.sentence: There is ___ use asking him — he never checks his messages.
gaps.explanation: 'There is no use doing something' = it is pointless.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with excuses; deliver on time or do not bother coming.
gaps.explanation: 'Has no patience with' — 'no' directly negates the noun.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the students has been given a personal timetable.
gaps.hint: this is the only option that can be followed by 'of' and take a singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each of the students has ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' here and 'all/both' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: ___ of what he says is nonsense.
gaps.explanation: 'Most of what he says' is the pattern 'most of + noun clause'; 'the most of' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: There weren't ___ chairs, so some guests had to stand.
gaps.explanation: 'Chairs' is countable and plural, so 'many' fits; 'much' and 'little' are for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: I haven't got ___ cash on me — I'll pay by card.
gaps.explanation: 'Any' is the normal quantifier in negative sentences; 'haven't got no cash' would be a double negative.

gaps.sentence: A large ___ of students have applied this year.
gaps.explanation: 'A large number of students' is used with countable plurals; 'amount' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: We haven't received ___ information about the delay.
gaps.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable, so 'much' is required in the negative sentence.
